ntlmContract.spnego: Fixed endpoint mechanism configuration, not inferred from bare HTTP Negotiate; NTLM MIC is distinct from SPNEGO mechListMIC

boundaryAssertions.beforeReceipt: No new receiver holding while packet is travelling
boundaryAssertions.beforeVerification: Receiving a proof/ciphertext is not accepting its meaning
boundaryAssertions.credentialDisclosure: Ordinary H password holding only after authInfo unwrap; later logon/resource denials do not erase it

boundaryAssertions.resource: New user/host identity and separate resource ACL; first hop stays valid on second-hop denial
boundaryAssertions.completedKey: mechanism-key remains C initiator subkey for AP-REQ/early client binding (AcceptorSubkey=0); acceptor-subkey belongs first to H at ap-reply and C only at mutual-verify. Completed reverse binding/authInfo and non-CredSSP WSMan use acceptor-subkey (AcceptorSubkey=1). AP-REP uses ticket-session-key; CredSSP WSMan body uses inner TLS.
boundaryAssertions.hostResourceKnowledge: resource-result gives H wire only. resource-result-accept verifies/unwraps/correlates and acquires plaintext before H learns success/denial or constructs WinRM output from exact accepted value. First-hop session and disclosed credentials persist on ACL denial.

boundaryAssertions.beforeReceipt: No new receiver holding while packet is travelling
boundaryAssertions.beforeVerification: Receiving a proof/ciphertext is not accepting its meaning
boundaryAssertions.credentialDisclosure: Ordinary H password holding only after authInfo unwrap; later logon/resource denials do not erase it
boundaryAssertions.session: CredSSP completion or RDP early-authorization result is not desktop/shell readiness
boundaryAssertions.resource: New user/host identity and separate resource ACL; first hop stays valid on second-hop denial
boundaryAssertions.completedKey: mechanism-key remains C initiator subkey for AP-REQ/early client binding (AcceptorSubkey=0); acceptor-subkey belongs first to H at ap-reply and C only at mutual-verify. Completed reverse binding/authInfo and non-CredSSP WSMan use acceptor-subkey (AcceptorSubkey=1). AP-REP uses ticket-session-key; CredSSP WSMan body uses inner TLS.
boundaryAssertions.hostResourceKnowledge: resource-result gives H wire only. resource-result-accept verifies/unwraps/correlates and acquires plaintext before H learns success/denial or constructs WinRM output from exact accepted value. First-hop session and disclosed credentials persist on ACL denial.

groupedOmissions: TLS handshake records grouped with explicit selected certificate and Finished validation; no invented new TLS PDU or computed runtime cryptography

TLS1.2 flights are grouped inner records, but each HTTP request/response boundary is explicit. ClientHello -> server flight -> client key-exchange/Finished -> server Finished; no unsolicited server HTTP response.
Command execution and output collection are explicitly one grouped command/receive request-response operation. Intermediate WSMan lifecycle traffic is omitted, not unsolicited HTTP output.
Protected-result integrity rejection is unsupported in this fixed valid-protection profile; no rejected result or fabricated successful command output is modeled.

boundaryAssertions.beforeReceipt: No new receiver holding while packet is travelling
boundaryAssertions.beforeVerification: Receiving a proof/ciphertext is not accepting its meaning
boundaryAssertions.credentialDisclosure: Ordinary H password holding only after authInfo unwrap; later logon/resource denials do not erase it
boundaryAssertions.session: CredSSP completion or RDP early-authorization result is not desktop/shell readiness
boundaryAssertions.resource: New user/host identity and separate resource ACL; first hop stays valid on second-hop denial
boundaryAssertions.http: AP-REP local construction is not receipt; final token shares the correlated response with its application body or CredSSP binding. Mutual proof is verified after receipt before use.
boundaryAssertions.clientKnowledge: Shell/output receipts create opaque holdings only. Client decoded shell handle and outcome knowledge begin at winrm-session-accept and winrm-command-accept respectively.
boundaryAssertions.completedKey: mechanism-key remains C initiator subkey for AP-REQ/early client binding (AcceptorSubkey=0); acceptor-subkey belongs first to H at ap-reply and C only at mutual-verify. Completed reverse binding/authInfo and non-CredSSP WSMan use acceptor-subkey (AcceptorSubkey=1). AP-REP uses ticket-session-key; CredSSP WSMan body uses inner TLS.
boundaryAssertions.hostResourceKnowledge: resource-result gives H wire only. resource-result-accept verifies/unwraps/correlates and acquires plaintext before H learns success/denial or constructs WinRM output from exact accepted value. First-hop session and disclosed credentials persist on ACL denial.

scenarios.failureKnowledge: Detecting actor first; remote actor only at its separately delivered failure
groupedOmissions: TLS handshake records grouped with explicit selected certificate and Finished validation; no invented new TLS PDU or computed runtime cryptography

TLS1.2 flights are grouped inner records, but each HTTP request/response boundary is explicit. ClientHello -> server flight -> client key-exchange/Finished -> server Finished; no unsolicited server HTTP response.
Command execution and output collection are explicitly one grouped command/receive request-response operation. Intermediate WSMan lifecycle traffic is omitted, not unsolicited HTTP output.
Protected-result integrity rejection is unsupported in this fixed valid-protection profile; no rejected result or fabricated successful command output is modeled.
scenarios.errata: Pinned editions incorporate previous published corrections; no extra erratum or live Windows behavior is inferred.

boundaryAssertions.beforeReceipt: No new receiver holding while packet is travelling
boundaryAssertions.beforeVerification: Receiving a proof/ciphertext is not accepting its meaning
boundaryAssertions.credentialDisclosure: Ordinary H password holding only after authInfo unwrap; later logon/resource denials do not erase it
boundaryAssertions.session: CredSSP completion or RDP early-authorization result is not desktop/shell readiness
boundaryAssertions.resource: New user/host identity and separate resource ACL; first hop stays valid on second-hop denial
boundaryAssertions.http: AP-REP local construction is not receipt; final token shares the correlated response with its application body or CredSSP binding. Mutual proof is verified after receipt before use.
boundaryAssertions.clientKnowledge: Shell/output receipts create opaque holdings only. Client decoded shell handle and outcome knowledge begin at winrm-session-accept and winrm-command-accept respectively.
boundaryAssertions.completedKey: mechanism-key remains C initiator subkey for AP-REQ/early client binding (AcceptorSubkey=0); acceptor-subkey belongs first to H at ap-reply and C only at mutual-verify. Completed reverse binding/authInfo and non-CredSSP WSMan use acceptor-subkey (AcceptorSubkey=1). AP-REP uses ticket-session-key; CredSSP WSMan body uses inner TLS.
boundaryAssertions.hostResourceKnowledge: resource-result gives H wire only. resource-result-accept verifies/unwraps/correlates and acquires plaintext before H learns success/denial or constructs WinRM output from exact accepted value. First-hop session and disclosed credentials persist on ACL denial.

scenarios.failureKnowledge: R authenticates user then denies ACL; first-hop session and delegated credentials remain
groupedOmissions: TLS handshake records grouped with explicit selected certificate and Finished validation; no invented new TLS PDU or computed runtime cryptography

TLS1.2 flights are grouped inner records, but each HTTP request/response boundary is explicit. ClientHello -> server flight -> client key-exchange/Finished -> server Finished; no unsolicited server HTTP response.
Command execution and output collection are explicitly one grouped command/receive request-response operation. Intermediate WSMan lifecycle traffic is omitted, not unsolicited HTTP output.
Protected-result integrity rejection is unsupported in this fixed valid-protection profile; no rejected result or fabricated successful command output is modeled.
scenarios.errata: Pinned editions incorporate previous published corrections; no extra erratum or live Windows behavior is inferred.

bindingContract.publicKeyInput: 270-byte DER RSAPublicKey SubjectPublicKey from the independent RFC7517 AppendixB public-certificate fixture, not294-byte SPKI, full certificate or thumbprint
bindingContract.scope: Symbolic protocol worksheet plus separately reproducible QA vectors; no live certificate trust claim

boundaryAssertions.beforeReceipt: No new receiver holding while packet is travelling
boundaryAssertions.beforeVerification: Receiving a proof/ciphertext is not accepting its meaning
boundaryAssertions.credentialDisclosure: Ordinary H password holding only after authInfo unwrap; later logon/resource denials do not erase it
boundaryAssertions.session: CredSSP completion or RDP early-authorization result is not desktop/shell readiness
boundaryAssertions.resource: New user/host identity and separate resource ACL; first hop stays valid on second-hop denial
boundaryAssertions.http: AP-REP local construction is not receipt; final token shares the correlated response with its application body or CredSSP binding. Mutual proof is verified after receipt before use.
boundaryAssertions.clientKnowledge: Shell/output receipts create opaque holdings only. Client decoded shell handle and outcome knowledge begin at winrm-session-accept and winrm-command-accept respectively.
boundaryAssertions.completedKey: mechanism-key remains C initiator subkey for AP-REQ/early client binding (AcceptorSubkey=0); acceptor-subkey belongs first to H at ap-reply and C only at mutual-verify. Completed reverse binding/authInfo and non-CredSSP WSMan use acceptor-subkey (AcceptorSubkey=1). AP-REP uses ticket-session-key; CredSSP WSMan body uses inner TLS.
boundaryAssertions.hostResourceKnowledge: resource-result gives H wire only. resource-result-accept verifies/unwraps/correlates and acquires plaintext before H learns success/denial or constructs WinRM output from exact accepted value. First-hop session and disclosed credentials persist on ACL denial.
